name: Scrambled Eggs and Toast
instructions: Whisk eggs with milk, salt, and pepper.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Add eggs and gently stir until softly set.
Toast bread and serve with the eggs.
notes: Add spinach, mushrooms, or cheddar if available.

name: Blueberry Oatmeal
instructions: Combine oats, milk, and cinnamon in a saucepan.
Simmer until creamy, stirring occasionally.
Stir in berries and cook for another minute.
Divide into bowls and drizzle with honey.
notes: Use water for part or all of the milk.

name: Pancakes
instructions: Mix pancake mix, milk, egg, and oil just until combined.
Heat a lightly greased skillet over medium heat.
Cook small rounds until bubbles form, then flip.
Cook until golden and serve with syrup.
notes: Do not overmix; a few small lumps are fine.

name: Breakfast Burritos
instructions: Dice potato, pepper, and onion.
Cook vegetables until tender and browned.
Add whisked eggs and cook until set.
Warm tortillas and fill with egg mixture, cheese, and salsa.
Roll into burritos.
notes: Cooked bacon or sausage can be added.

name: Berry Yogurt Parfaits
instructions: Thaw berries slightly if frozen solid.
Layer yogurt, berries, and granola.
Drizzle with honey and serve.
notes: Keep granola separate until serving if making ahead.

name: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup
instructions: Simmer tomato sauce, broth, milk, garlic powder, and Italian seasoning for 10 minutes.
Butter one side of each bread slice and place cheese between the unbuttered sides.
Cook sandwiches until golden and cheese melts.
Serve with hot soup.
notes: Use vegetable broth for a vegetarian version.

name: Tuna Salad Sandwiches
instructions: Drain tuna.
Chop pickles and celery.
Mix tuna, mayonnaise, mustard, pickles, and celery.
Serve on bread with lettuce.
notes: Chopped onion can replace some of the celery.

name: Chicken Salad Sandwiches
instructions: Cook chicken until it reaches 165°F.
Cool and chop the chicken.
Mix with mayonnaise, mustard, celery, and pickles.
Serve on bread with lettuce.
notes: Leftover cooked chicken works very well.

name: Chicken Quesadillas
instructions: Cook and slice the chicken.
Cook pepper and onion until tender.
Fill tortillas with cheese, chicken, and vegetables.
Cook folded tortillas until crisp and cheese melts.
Serve with salsa and sour cream.
notes: Leftover chicken can replace freshly cooked chicken.

name: Black Bean Quesadillas
instructions: Drain and rinse beans.
Mix beans with corn, cumin, and a little salsa.
Fill tortillas with bean mixture and cheese.
Cook until crisp and cheese melts.
Serve with remaining salsa.
notes: Canned corn works just as well as fresh.

name: Chicken Tacos
instructions: Cut chicken into bite-size pieces.
Cook with taco seasoning until done.
Warm tortillas.
Fill with chicken, lettuce, tomato, cheese, and sour cream.
Finish with lime juice.
notes: Chicken thighs are a less expensive alternative.

name: Beef Tacos
instructions: Brown beef and drain excess fat if needed.
Add taco seasoning and required water.
Simmer until thickened.
Warm tortillas and fill with beef, lettuce, tomato, cheese, and salsa.

name: Beef and Bean Chili
instructions: Brown beef and onion in a large pot.
Add garlic and cook briefly.
Stir in tomatoes, beans, tomato paste, broth, chili powder, and cumin.
Simmer uncovered for 30 to 40 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
notes: Excellent for freezing; chili thickens as it cools.

name: Spaghetti with Meat Sauce
instructions: Cook spaghetti according to package directions.
Brown beef and onion.
Add garlic and cook briefly.
Add tomato sauce, tomato paste, and Italian seasoning.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Serve over spaghetti with Parmesan.
notes: Double the sauce and freeze the extra.

name: Creamy Chicken Alfredo
instructions: Cook pasta, adding broccoli during the final few minutes.
Cook seasoned chicken and slice it.
Melt butter and briefly cook garlic.
Add milk and cream cheese and stir until smooth.
Stir in Parmesan and simmer gently.
Toss pasta and broccoli with sauce and top with chicken.
notes: Avoid aggressively boiling the cheese sauce or it may separate.

name: Baked Ziti
instructions: Cook pasta until just shy of tender.
Brown sausage and add garlic.
Add tomato sauce and Italian seasoning and simmer 10 minutes.
Combine pasta with most of the sauce and mozzarella.
Transfer to a baking dish and top with remaining sauce, mozzarella, and Parmesan.
Bake at 375°F until bubbling and browned.
notes: Rest 5 to 10 minutes before serving.

name: Easy Mac and Cheese
instructions: Cook macaroni and drain.
Melt butter and whisk in flour; cook 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk and simmer until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in cheddar.
Combine with macaroni and season.
notes: Add broccoli, peas, or leftover chicken for a fuller meal.

name: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry
instructions: Cook or reheat rice.
Cook bite-size chicken in a hot skillet.
Add peppers and frozen vegetables and stir-fry until crisp-tender.
Add garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes.
Serve over rice.
notes: Swap the frozen vegetables for broccoli, peas, or corn.

name: Chicken Fried Rice
instructions: Use cold cooked rice if possible.
Cook diced chicken and set aside.
Cook onion and carrot, then add peas.
Scramble eggs in the same skillet.
Add rice and chicken and stir-fry until hot.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil.
notes: Cold leftover rice produces the best texture.

name: Sheet-Pan Chicken, Potatoes, and Carrots
instructions: Heat oven to 425°F.
Cut vegetables into similar-sized pieces and toss with oil and half the seasonings.
Season chicken and arrange everything on a sheet pan.
Roast until vegetables are tender and chicken reaches 165°F.
notes: Leave space between pieces so the vegetables roast instead of steam.

name: Pork Chops with Mashed Potatoes
instructions: Boil cubed potatoes until tender.
Season pork chops with paprika, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Sear pork chops in olive oil until cooked through.
Mash potatoes with butter, milk, and garlic.
Rest pork chops briefly before serving.
notes: Use a thermometer and avoid overcooking the pork.

name: Garlic Butter Shrimp Pasta
instructions: Cook pasta and reserve some pasta water.
Melt butter and briefly cook garlic and red pepper flakes.
Add shrimp and cook until opaque.
Add pasta, Parmesan, lemon juice, and pasta water.
Toss until glossy and finish with parsley.
notes: Shrimp overcook quickly; remove from heat as soon as they are opaque.

name: Baked Salmon with Rice and Broccoli
instructions: Heat oven to 400°F and cook rice.
Brush salmon with olive oil and season.
Bake salmon until it flakes easily, about 12 to 15 minutes.
Steam or roast broccoli.
Serve salmon with rice and broccoli and finish with lemon.
notes: Keep the salmon moist by avoiding unnecessary overcooking.

name: Chicken Noodle Soup
instructions: Cook diced onion, carrots, and celery until slightly softened.
Add garlic and cook briefly.
Add broth, chicken, and thyme and simmer until chicken is cooked.
Remove and shred chicken, then return it to the pot.
Add noodles and cook until tender.
Season to taste.
notes: For better leftovers, cook noodles separately and add them to individual servings.

name: Creamy Potato Soup
instructions: Cook onion and celery in butter until softened.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in broth and milk.
Add potatoes and simmer until tender.
Mash some potatoes against the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in cheddar and season.
notes: Use vegetable broth for a vegetarian version.

name: Chickpea Salad Pitas
instructions: Drain and rinse chickpeas.
Mash about half with a fork and leave the rest whole.
Mix with mayonnaise and Dijon.
Dice cucumber and tomato and fold them in.
Fill pitas with the mixture and lettuce.
notes: Greek yogurt can replace some or all of the mayonnaise.

name: Loaded Baked Potatoes
instructions: Bake pierced potatoes at 425°F until tender, about 45 to 50 minutes.
Cook bacon until crisp and crumble it.
Split potatoes and fluff with butter.
Top with cheddar, sour cream, bacon, and green onion.
notes: Use broccoli instead of bacon for a vegetarian variation.

name: Peanut Butter Oat Energy Bites
instructions: Mix peanut butter and honey until smooth.
Stir in oats, raisins, chocolate chips, and cinnamon.
Chill briefly if the mixture is too sticky.
Roll into small balls and refrigerate until firm.
notes: Keep refrigerated; these are intended as a snack rather than a meal replacement.

name: Vegetable Pasta Primavera
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions.
Sauté chopped vegetables in olive oil until crisp-tender.
Add garlic and cook briefly.
Toss pasta with vegetables and Parmesan.
Season and serve.
notes: Frozen broccoli can replace fresh broccoli.

name: Honey Mustard Chicken
instructions: Whisk Dijon, honey, olive oil, garlic powder, and pepper.
Coat chicken with half the sauce.
Cook chicken in a skillet until browned and cooked through.
Brush with remaining sauce during the last few minutes.
Rest briefly before serving.
notes: Serve with rice, potatoes, or vegetables from the inventory.

name: Chocolate Oatmeal Cookies
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F.
Cream butter and brown sugar.
Beat in egg and vanilla.
Mix flour, oats, baking soda, and cocoa separately.
Stir dry ingredients into the butter mixture and fold in chocolate chips.
Bake spoonfuls for 10 to 12 minutes.
Cool briefly before transferring.
notes: Cookies should look slightly underdone in the center when removed.
